All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Part Time – Senior, Hazardous Waste Safety and Environmental Specialist – Portland, Oregon

Introduction

Are you a highly motivated self-starter seeking to join a growth-focused Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) consulting firm? Are you looking for a company that will provide interesting and technically challenging work and will also invest in your development and grow your professional skills? If so, consider a career with Apex. Powered by strong sales, extraordinary client retention, multiple career path options, strategic acquisitions, and an entrepreneurial spirit, Apex Companies is one of the fastest growing EHS consulting firms in the USA. We take pride in meeting and exceeding our clients’ expectations and have earned numerous industry awards for project excellence. We continue to grow, and we want you to grow with us.

Role Overview

This role is to provide overarching Hazardous Waste and Environmental Safety expertise to one of Apex’s most valued clients, a national aerospace manufacturer. Over the last 2 decades Apex has worked hand and hand with the national aerospace manufacturer helping them achieve their occupational health and safety, ergonomic, environmental and engineering goals. The incumbent will serve as a Hazardous Waste and Environmental Specialist to support site-wide hazardous waste and environmental compliance operations. This is a part time role with up to 40 hours a week based on client’s request.

The incumbent will be dedicated full time to supporting the sites hazardous waste and environmental compliance operations. The individual in this role will work closely with environmental, engineering, maintenance, leadership, and EHS stakeholders to assist with closing any and all hazardous waste and compliance gaps identified as well as supporting the day-to-day operations.

Key Responsibilities

Project Background

Hazardous waste background, including familiarity with Oregon’s Dangerous and Hazardous Waste regulations
Familiar with EPA hazardous and dangerous waste regulations
Familiar with related records (manifests, hazardous waste invoices, MSD, etc.)
Environmental compliance-oriented
Able to conduct walking inspections of RCRA accumulation/satellite areas
able to document and photograph areas of concern, then develop professional emails to convey desired mitigation
able to conduct follow-up inspections to ensure corrective measures were implemented
DOT trained -- desirable, but not required, and they would not be expected to sign manifests
Reasonable computer skills (data entry, email, able to pick up basic operations on the client’s internal data base and programs.
Able to work as part of a team with client’s current Environmental employees dedicated to hazardous waste compliance at the site.

Scope of Work

Factory Dust Disposal Project
Sampling
Tracking (locations & disposal requests)
Site Inspections – Small Quantity Generators
Land Disposal Restrictions - Review/Update Project Support
Battery Collection Location Updates w/HazMat
RCRA Inspection Forms - compile, organize
Invoice Reviews & Approvals
Hazmat ECTs HW trainings – help develop a mini training program on regulatory compliance and policies at the site.
Visit crew meetings to train individuals or very small groups on policies, program aspects, compliance, etc
Ability to give small presentations is desirable but not required – we can do the presentations if needed

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, environmental, waste management, chemical or a related technical discipline required.
Minimum 15 years of progressive hazardous waste and or waste management, engineering, environmental/hazardous waste compliance. (Experience and education will be accounted for appropriately).
40 hour HAZWOPER
Desired but not required:
OSHA 30
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)
Certified Professional in Waste Management (CPWM)
Hazardous Waste Management Specialist (HMS)
Excellent communication, training, technical writing, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and standard safety documentation and reporting practices.
Valid driver’s license required.

Select Key Performance Indicators

Demonstrates the ability to work independently, successfully executing technical projects with minimal supervision.
Customer needs are met on a timely basis and emergencies are responded to quickly.
Meets annually established goals for personally-generated revenue, and utilization %.
Meets annually established goals for Customer satisfaction.
Pursues ongoing professional development as mutually agreed with the Business Unit Manager.

Why Join Apex

Apex Companies is a strong place to build an environmental and EHS career. You will get meaningful, hands on work with diverse clients, the backing of an experienced national team, and clear opportunities to grow your technical and leadership skills. You’re exposed to projects that span industrial hygiene, hazardous waste, stormwater, and environmental compliance, so your day to day work stays challenging and relevant. At the same time, Apex emphasizes collaboration, mentorship, and professional development, making it easier to pursue advanced certifications and long term career goals while contributing to projects that genuinely protect people and the environment.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
About This Role

We are currently seeking an experienced Environment Specialist to join the Asset Retirement HSE team of a leading global oil & gas organisation.

This is a 2-year contract opportunity working on a FIFO 2 weeks on / 2 weeks off roster, providing hands-on environmental support across a major Asset Retirement program encompassing decommissioning, remediation, well abandonment and associated project activities.

Reporting to the HSE Team Lead - Asset Retirement, you will work closely with project teams, contractors, operational personnel and environmental specialists to support the safe, compliant and environmentally responsible delivery of Asset Retirement activities.

The Role

The Environment Specialist will provide practical environmental guidance and assurance across field-based operations and projects, with a strong focus on environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities will include:

Conducting field-based environmental assurance, verification and validation activities across Asset Retirement worksites.
Supporting environmental monitoring and sampling programs covering air, water, waste and soil.
Providing support across waste management, fauna handling and other environmental field activities.
Supporting environmental risk assessments and the implementation of appropriate controls.
Developing and delivering environmental training, awareness initiatives and environmental leadership programs.
Supporting teams and contractors to build environmental capability and improve environmental performance.
Participating in projects and working groups relating to environmental risk, waste management, contaminated land, rehabilitation and continuous improvement.
Building effective working relationships across HSE, project teams, contractors, business partners, regulators and corporate environmental teams.
Supporting environmental regulatory approvals, compliance obligations, audits and reporting requirements.
Participating in Incident Management and Emergency Response activities, including emergency exercises and response events.
Supporting environmental and wildlife response activities where required.
Facilitating incident investigations and learning events using recognised methodologies including 5-Why, SAFE, Why-Tree and Learning Teams.
Applying Human and Organizational Performance (HOP) principles to support sustainable improvements in environmental and HSE performance.

Requirements

To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally have:

A Diploma or Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience applying environmental management systems and environmental risk management principles in a practical operational or project environment.
Strong field-based environmental experience and the ability to provide practical advice to frontline personnel and contractors.
Excellent stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
The confidence to operate as a visible HSE professional and engage effectively with leaders, frontline workers, contractors and regulators.
Strong communication skills with the ability to adapt your approach to different stakeholder groups.
The ability and willingness to work a FIFO 2:2 roster.
You must have current right to work in Australia to be considered for this role

Experience in some or all of the following will be highly regarded:

Environmental assurance, compliance,monitoring and sampling
Contaminated land management and remediation.
Waste management.
Fauna handling.
Emergency response and oil spill response..
Major projects, construction or operational environments.
Decommissioning, remediation or Asset Retirement activities.

Benefits

Work for a global oil and gas business
FIFO 2:2 roster
2 year contract
Salary sacrificing
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Corporate discounts

**Overview**  
We are seeking a highly motivated Cleanroom Environmental Monitoring Technicians to join our team in PAL's Microbiology \& EM services for Biotech, Pharma, medical device, and Compounding Pharmacies companies. The positions are temporary with potential for becoming regular employee later on. This role is essential in ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and maintaining the integrity of our laboratory processes. Services include validation of clean rooms, water systems and compressed gases systems, and routine sampling of these systems. Requirements

* Minimum AS degree in science with a concentration in microbiology. The position requires at least 1 year of hands\-on experience in microbiology or EM testing in an FDA GMP regulated.
* Hands on experience in endotoxin testing, cleanroom Environmental monitoring, water testing and USP microbial methods.

* Excellent organizational skills along with good written and verbal communication skills in English.
* Ability to follow instructions and work as a team member.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Ability to start early (6am), work overtime and weekends as needed to complete projects.

* Must pass background check and drug testing.

Senior/Associate Consultant - Land Quality & Remediation - Perth

About The Business And Role

At SLR our purpose is to Make Sustainability Happen. SLR is an international environmental consultancy with a globally recognised reputation for providing high quality tailored services. With 1000+ staff in APAC alone, we are proud to be one of the small number of leading international specialist environmental consultancies.

We have an opportunity for an experienced Contaminated Land Consultant to join our Perth office on a permanent full-time basis.

Reporting to the Team Lead, you will be given the opportunity to lead and assist in contaminated land and remediation assessments and projects, working alongside supports locally and across APAC. We pride in delivering contaminated land services at a high standard. This role has potential to develop further into a formal team leadership role depending on the right candidate.

Develop and deliver a high standard of technically sound reports with minimal technical review and correction required. (PSI, SAQP, DSI, RAPs, validation reports in line with QA/QC requirements)
Undertake and lead occasional fieldwork and support the training and development of junior staff across soil, soil vapour, sediment, surface water, groundwater, and landfill gas sampling, as well as well installation and logging.
Develop strong relationships externally with clients, to provide competent project management of moderate size and effectively lead project teams
Develop proposals, bids and tenders as required
Display confidence in data analysis, interpretation and management with solid technical writing capability.
Work seamlessly in a team environment across multidisciplinary projects and provide oversight and mentoring to a growing LQR team
Committed to our core principles in health and safety, and environment and sustainability.

A professional qualification in environmental science, engineering, geology, hydrogeology, soil science or other earth science related degree.
Between 8-12+ years of experience in a similar role across consulting services in Australia.

A high level of commercial acumen and proven success in developing winning proposals and client relationship management.

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal – particularly across report writing and computer literacy.
Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work efficiently in teams.

Full and unrestricted working rights in Australia.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast\-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we'd like to talk with you about growing with us.


EnSafe is seeking a full\-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego, CA, office.



This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.


**What we are looking for**



An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You'll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.



Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.


***Key responsibilities of this position include***


***What you will be doing:***


* Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
* Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
* Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
* Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
* Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
* Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
* Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
* Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
* Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
* Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
* Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
* Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.


***Minimum Skills and Requirements***


* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
* Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
* Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
* Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
* Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
* Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
* Ability to manage schedules, budgets, client expectations, and multiple concurrent assignments.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong critical\-thinking and problem\-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel to support project work.
* Valid driver's license and ability to perform field activities associated with environmental site assessments.


***Preferred Qualifications***


***The following experience would be beneficial but is not required:***


* Experience managing Phase I ESA programs or providing technical/peer review.
* Qualification as an Environmental Professional under ASTM/AAI requirements.
* Phase II ESA, subsurface investigation, soil, groundwater, or vapor assessment experience.
* Environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste, hazardous materials, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, CERS/HMBP, or EPCRA/Tier II reporting.
* Experience supporting industrial, commercial real estate, logistics/warehouse, energy, municipal, or similar clients.
* Professional Geologist (PG), Professional Engineer (PE), or other relevant professional certification.
* Building sciences or hazardous building materials experience.
* Experience with asbestos\-containing materials, lead\-based paint, mold/microbial assessments, or related building surveys.
* California asbestos or lead certifications.
* 40\-hour HAZWOPER training.


**Why Join EnSafe?**


* **Employee\-Owned Advantage**  

EnSafe is 100% employee\-owned, with an ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) since 1997\. That means when EnSafe succeeds, you succeed too, turning company growth directly into shared rewards.
* **Commitment to Growth and Wellness**  

The company supports personalized career development, mentorship, and employee wellness initiatives such as health tracking tools.
* **Purpose‑Driven Work**  

EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long\-standing technical credibility.
* **Safety as a Value, Not Just a Service**  

Safety is deeply embedded in our culture, prioritizing employee well\-being in addition to helping clients maintain compliance. We stress that *"safety is part of everything we do."*
* **A Culture of Freedom \& Ownership**  

At EnSafe, our career philosophy is built on freedom. The freedom to take initiative, achieve your goals, and shape your own career path Employees are encouraged to pursue growth in a flexible, entrepreneurial environment.
* **Challenging, Creative Work**  

Workdays at EnSafe are anything but ordinary,

jobs.title: Early Career Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**This Opportunity**
--------------------

WSP is currently initiating a search for an Early Career Environmental Scientist for our Portland, OR office. Be involved in projects with our Advisory \& Planning Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our clients’ objectives and solves their challenges.


Takes part in providing local technical assistance for the collection, identification, and compiling of observational and spatial data concerning a variety of biological, physical, and earth sciences. Provides local assistance for the development of processes and infrastructure relating to water supply, air emission, pollution control, cultural impact, and preserving the quality of the environment by identifying, controlling, and preventing disruption to environmental systems and species caused by human activity. Generates accurate and concise documentation, ensuring that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.


**Your Impact**
---------------

* Under general supervision, conduct natural resource field surveys collecting observational, spatial, and environmental data.
* Under general supervision, collect and compile samples of air, soil, water, sludge, and other matrices for analysis.
* Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurement and documentation.
* Assist with performing basic professional environmental science work relating to ecological systems, air, and water resources, assisting with verifying the characteristics of a site and providing entry\-level technical assistance on various environmental issues.
* Generate complete, accurate, and concise documentation using electronic systems and field/work site notebook.
* Comply with safety guidelines and site\-specific procedures which include but are not limited to, the maintenance of sample collection, location data, laboratory or statistical documentation, and logbooks.
* Utilize the latest technologies and techniques in performing studies and analysis of habitats, sites, and potential impacts to the health of the environment and the population.
* Complete training on assigned tasks.
* Exercise responsible and ethical decision\-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
* Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

**Who You Are**
---------------

jobs.description:
About Tower Semiconductor

Looking for a career path in the high-tech industry? Become part of a team focused on delivering the most exciting semiconductor technology in the world! If you enjoy working with others in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and are looking for an opportunity to grow your career in this exciting industry, then Tower Semiconductor is the place to be!

Tower Semiconductor, the leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, provides technology, development, and process platforms for analog integrated circuits to more than 300 customers worldwide across growing markets such as communications, mobile, infrastructure, consumer, industrial, automotive, medical, and aerospace and defense, among others.

Join Tower and become part of a dynamic organization with exceptionally talented and dedicated team members who work collaboratively to provide best-in-class technological solutions to our clients.

Job Description

An Environmental Specialist is responsible for ensuring uninterrupted manufacturing operations through proactive environmental compliance, risk identification, regulatory engagement, and timely execution of critical Environmental programs. The role supports semiconductor manufacturing operations by ensuring compliance with environmental regulations governing air emissions, wastewater treatment, hazardous waste management, and chemical handling.

This position works closely with manufacturing, facilities, engineering, operations, and corporate EHS teams to minimize environmental risk, maintain regulatory compliance, and support safe and reliable fab operations.

This Job Is For You If

You can ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations (e.g., 40 CFR, 30 TAC) related to air emissions, hazardous waste, wastewater, stormwater, and chemical management.
You can proactively identify compliance risks, operational vulnerabilities, and permitting gaps, and escalate issues early to management with clear mitigation plans.
You can maintain accurate environmental records, emissions inventories, permit tracking systems, and regulatory submissions to ensure timely and compliant reporting
You can oversee hazardous waste management, hazardous material shipping, and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) programs.
You can manage air compliance programs including stack testing, Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR), greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, and criteria pollutant tracking.
You can monitor wastewater treatment systems and implement Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP).
You can lead regulatory inspections and agency interactions with professionalism, technical competence, and strong preparation.
You can conduct facility audits and inspections of chemical storage, waste accumulation, and environmental control systems.
You can investigate environmental incidents, determine root causes, and drive timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
You can coordinate effectively across operations, facilities, engineering, production, and corporate EHS teams to ensure alignment and execution of environmental priorities.
You can develop and maintain environmental procedures, standards, and training programs to ensure ongoing compliance and operational readiness.
You can prepare and submit environmental reports including Toxic Release Inventory (TRI), Tier II, emissions inventories, and Discharge Monitoring Reports.
You can implement programs that minimize environmental risk, business interruption, and operational impact.
You can manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while maintaining high accuracy, responsiveness, and attention to detail.

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Safety and Health, or a related field required.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance experience, preferably within semiconductor manufacturing or other highly regulated industrial operations.
Extensive knowledge of environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and regulatory reporting.
Experience managing environmental compliance programs related to air, waste, water, and hazardous materials.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, and project management skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and environmental tracking/reporting systems.
Ability to conduct inspections in manufacturing and industrial environments.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 pounds as needed.
Ability to sit, stand, walk, and work on a computer for extended periods as required by the role.

Preferred Characteristics

Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Proactive communicator with excellent follow-through
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Comfortable operating in high-visibility, high-responsibility environments
Strong cross-functional collaboration and coordination skills
High attention to detail and strong organizational discipline

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned environmental, water resources, and engineering consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. The PFAS Program Manager will serve as a catalyst for collaboration across EKI’s PFAS practitioners and will help connect technical capabilities with client and market needs. The role combines technical project execution, practice development, internal coordination, client engagement, and business development. Success in the position will require strong technical judgement, the ability to work effectively with and leverage EKI’s subject-matter experts, and the leadership and initiative to build a coordinated and effective PFAS practice.

Advance EKI's PFAS practice by bringing together PFAS practitioners across the company; fostering and promoting knowledge sharing; developing training programs; supporting recruitment of PFAS professionals; identifying technical capabilities, resource needs, and capability gaps; and helping establish priorities and initiatives for continued development of the practice.

Strengthen EKI’s external visibility and reputation in PFAS through client and regulatory engagement; technical publications and presentations; industry conferences, technical committees, and other external forums.

jobs.description:
Title: EHS Specialist

Locations: Mountain View, CA (Fully Onsite)

Duration: Contract (6+ Months - Extendable)

Client: Aviation & Aerospace domain

Job Description:

We are seeking EHS Specialists (Contractors) to join our team. The goal of this position is to support the hands-on deployment, execution, and monitoring of practical EHS programs, ensuring our day-to-day workplace operations actively embody our core cultural behavior: “Safety Is Our Cornerstone.” You will join the EHS team, working boots on the ground to maintain total regulatory compliance and evaluate hazard points across our fast-paced aerospace environments.
Due to the nature of the work required for this position, this is an onsite opportunity. You will be required to work from our Mountain View, CA office, with flexibility to support or travel to local remote facilities as required by operational needs.
In this role you will own the day-to-day practical execution of core environmental, health, and safety protocols across R&D, Engineering, laboratories, and advanced manufacturing spaces.
As a mid-level specialist, you will bridge the gap between high-level policy and real-world implementation by conducting routine field audits, managing chemical and hazardous waste inventories, and facilitating employee safety training. You will collaborate directly with engineers, technicians, and floor operators to perform Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and incident investigations and ensure proper risk mitigation is in place. You will be instrumental in fostering a transparent, "Just Culture" workspace that enables cutting-edge aerospace development to proceed safely.

What you will do:

You will provide critical boots on the ground EHS support for our Bay Area facilities, helping to deploy specialized EHS solutions tailored to advanced air taxi development.
You will manage and maintain daily ownership over core workplace safety programs including Injury and Illness Prevention Plans (IIPP), Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Machine Guarding, Respiratory Protection, Electrical Safety/NFPA 70e, and Powered Industrial Trucks.
You will support Engineering, Manufacturing, R&D, and Flight Test teams by conducting proactive Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs).
Executing field industrial hygiene assessments/sampling, including coordination with qualified third-party consultants.
You will help solve complex floor-level problems surrounding hazardous material classifications, maintaining updated Safety Data Sheet (SDS) documentation, and updating Hazardous Materials Business Plans (HMBP) via CERS.
You will routinely audit facilities, equipment, and work processes to identify structural risks, draft detailed inspection reports tracking corrective actions, and ensure timely closure of audit findings.
You will prepare, schedule, and lead instructor-led EHS training sessions, while actively participating in the internal Safety Collective .
You will lead responses to emergency situations onsite, such as fires (including from li-ion thermal runaway), electrical safety incidents, and other potential emergencies.

Requirements:

B.S. or B.A. in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, Industrial Hygiene, or a related field with 5+ years of dedicated experience performing EHS duties in an industrial, hardware R&D, or manufacturing environment.
You have solid, applied knowledge of Cal-OSHA, federal OSHA standards, EPA requirements, and localized environmental regulatory baselines.
DOT / CA title 22 (Div. 4.5) for hazwaste management/signing manifests or ability to gain certification.
You have practical experience conducting accident/incident root-cause investigations, implementing corrective actions, and writing up standard compliance documentation.
You are certified or have the documented willingness to complete immediate DOT training to properly sign hazardous and universal waste manifests.
You are highly proficient with modern inspection technologies, workplace data tracking equipment, and standard office software applications.
You have strong interpersonal skills to influence internal customers.
Physically able to walk manufacturing and laboratory floors daily, conduct rigorous facility audits, and comfortably handle or carry related inspection and safety equipment.
Available to occasionally work flexible hours outside the standard workweek (including early mornings, evenings, or weekends) to support specialized systems test, flight test and manufacturing tasks or active incident investigations.
Experience in manufacturing or R&D environments preferred.

BayOne is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any federal, state, or local protected class.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced air quality professional to provide technical leadership and project delivery support within Ramboll’s Air and Climate Service Line. This position will focus on complex air dispersion modelling, air quality impact assessment, client advisory services, project management, and mentoring of junior to mid-level colleagues.

The role offers an opportunity to contribute to a growing national air quality practice while working collaboratively across Australian and global teams. Candidates with experience in digital tools, data workflows, automation, GIS, or cross-region technical coordination will be well placed to support ongoing innovation in how air quality services are delivered.

Air Quality Managing Consultant

Working within the Air and Climate Service Line you will be responsible for identifying, conducting and developing air quality projects based on an understanding of business needs, challenges, opportunities and the marketplace. Ramboll is seeking an experienced Air Quality Modelling professional for this position. Our ideal candidate is a technical leader with a proven track record of managing complex, multi-faceted air quality modelling projects, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a trusted advisor to clients. You would be responsible for overseeing project staff and be responsible for project delivery across the air quality team.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Technical Leadership: Lead and deliver complex air quality dispersion modelling and environmental impact assessment projects using regulatory and specialist models such as AERMOD, CALPUFF, CALMET, GRAL/GRAMM, TAPM and WRF. Develop innovative approaches to solving complex air quality, odour, emissions inventory and post-processing challenges.
Project Management: Manage air quality projects, including scope, schedule, budget, resources and quality, to support on-time and on-budget delivery that meets client expectations. Supervise project teams and delegate tasks to junior staff as required.
Technical Review and Quality Assurance: Provide senior-level QA/QC review and technical oversight of modelling analyses, emissions inventories, impact assessments, management plans, approval inputs and technical reports prepared by project teams.
Client and Regulatory Engagement: Act as a trusted client advisor through the full project lifecycle, from early strategy and scoping through approvals, compliance and implementation. Lead or support technical discussions with regulators and approval authorities on behalf of clients.
Staff Mentoring and Development: Mentor junior to mid-level air quality staff by providing technical guidance, training, review and career development support.
Business Development: Contribute technical and business content to proposals, develop scopes of work, support strategic client engagement and identify opportunities for growth in air quality services.
Digital and Cross-Region Collaboration: Support efficient project delivery through digital and technical innovation coordinating with Australian, APAC and global colleagues where specialist input or shared capability is required.

You will be part of the Australian Air and Climate Service Line working within the Air Quality Team as a Managing Consultant. You will lead the delivery of air quality projects, providing technical leadership, project management, and mentoring to junior team members, while supporting the ongoing growth and development of Ramboll’s national air quality capability.

Reporting to the National Air and Climate Practice Lead, you will play a key role in strengthening Ramboll’s air quality services and contributing to the continued success of the team. The position offers the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across Australia, APAC and our global network to enhance project delivery, provide specialist technical expertise, drive digital innovation and promote technical excellence across Ramboll’s national air quality team.

Qualifications

About You

From the moment you start we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills and capabilities that will set you up for success:

Bachelor or Post Graduate degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering or related field with minimum 10 years of experience in air dispersion modelling and impact assessment.
Certified Air Quality Professional (CAQP) with the Clean Air Society of Australia and New Zealand and demonstrated involvement in profile raising activities (preferred).
Proficiency in meteorological and air dispersion modelling software such as AERMET, AERMOD, CALMET, CALPUFF, GRAMM, GRAL, TAPM and WRF.
Experience in development of air, odour and GHG emissions inventories across a wide range of industry sectors.
Strong technical knowledge and report writing skills, including preparation of Air Quality Impact Assessments, monitoring reports, Air Quality Management Plans and proposals.
Experienced project management skills, including direct client engagement. Business development skills are highly desirable, as is demonstrated experience in people management and/or mentoring.
Experience in ambient air quality monitoring, stack testing knowledge, climate risk assessment and/or noise monitoring and modelling, is not essential but would be highly regarded.
Experience in the following fields is highly desirable, including GIS software (e.g. ArcGIS Pro and Surfer), programming (e.g. R and Python), and analytical and data visualisation platforms (e.g. MS Power BI).
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical, digital or data-related information clearly to clients, regulators and multidisciplinary project teams.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Interesting and diverse projects
The opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest professionals in your field
Flexible work arrangements
Investment in your development
Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles
Appreciation for the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics. Please let us know if there are any changes, we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

The Water Resources Project Manager position reports to the Team Leader (TL) and is responsible for project management and technical oversight of high-impact projects with California clients from initial project planning through implementation. Point of Contact for client; coordinate and lead client meetings and related meetings and coordination with external parties
Plan, organize, and manage staff to deliver quality project work products on time and within budget
Prepare effective presentations that efficiently communicate complex technical concepts to a broad audience

Provide quality assurance and quality control on and review of project deliverables

Other duties as required

Job Posting: Central Region Office Supervisor



Department of Food \& Agriculture


JC\-527593* 

Central Region Office Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/24/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**


Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) (SES) is responsible for overseeing the operations of the Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch Central Region Office in Fresno, California. The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision of Environmental Scientists that conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and milk processing plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairies, processing plants, haulers and other dairy food facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard or unsafe dairy products to California consumers.  

  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this position are primarily conducted indoors approximately 80% of the time. The incumbent has an office in the Central Regional Office located in Downtown Fresno. The office is furnished with all the necessary equipment for job performance and function.  

Incumbents must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted during the course of the work, work well under pressure, make appropriate decisions and recommendations, work independently to complete assignments and meet deadlines.  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual dairy farm premises to complex, multi\-story processing plants complexes.  

Occasional travel (including nights and weekends) may be required for meetings, events, and field support as needed. A state issued vehicle may be assigned to drive on state business.  

The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

### **Department Information**


The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.


The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMP’s) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in\-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. Branch personnel provide training and supervision for county Approved Milk Inspection Services and conduct ratings and inspections of farms, processors, and manufacturers of single\-service dairy containers for compliance with requirements of the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ensure approval of California dairy products in interstate commerce. In addition, the Branch ensures that commercial laboratory testing used to determine the basis of payment for milk or for screening of milk for drug residues prior to processing is conducted according to required methods to protect consumers and the marketplace.

Element Concord has a current opening for an Equipment Manager/Environmental Monitoring Manager
to join our growing team. The Equipment Management/Environmental Monitoring Manager
is responsible for leading Element Concord’s Cleanroom Services, Equipment Management programs, and client Environmental Monitoring (EM) services. This role oversees department operations, personnel training and development, technical execution, client communication, and compliance with applicable quality, client, and regulatory requirements. $90k-$110k DOE

LEADERSHIP AND DEPARTMENT MANAGEMENT

Manage equipment lifecycle activities in support of equipment calibration, validation, and PM activities
Support personnel training, qualifications, mentoring, workload planning, and development to ensure assigned duties are performed competently and consistently
Promote a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and compliance with Element policies and procedures
Ensure departmental activities are prioritized and completed in alignment with client commitments, internal timelines, and business needs

Ensure equipment used for laboratory and cleanroom operations remains appropriately maintained, documented, and suitable for use

Support equipment-related investigations, change controls, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives

ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND CLEANROOM SERVICES

Ensure monitoring and laboratory activities are performed in compliance with applicable quality system, regulatory, and data integrity expectations
Oversee preparation, review, and execution of protocols, procedures, forms, and reports associated with Environmental Monitoring and cleanroom operations
Review Environmental Monitoring data, trends, deviations, and excursions and support timely investigation, corrective action, and effectiveness activities as applicable
Support cleanroom qualification, requalification, contamination control, and operational readiness activities as required

QUALITY, COMPLIANCE, AND DOCUMENTATION

Ensure department activities comply with the Quality Manual, applicable SOPs, client requirements, and relevant regulatory expectations
Maintain documentation practices consistent with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and data integrity requirements
Support internal audits, client audits, regulatory inspections, and quality system assessments within the department’s scope
Review and support SOPs, protocols, reports, deviations, CAPAs, and change controls associated with Environmental Monitoring, cleanroom services, and equipment management

CLIENT COMMUNICATION AND BUSINESS PERFORMANCE

Communicate professionally with clients to discuss project requirements, resolve issues, support customer satisfaction, and maintain strong business relationships
Ensure efficient departmental operations and support achievement of revenue, EBITDA, productivity, and service delivery objectives
Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen compliance, efficiency, turnaround time, and customer experience

Required Qualifications

Strong organizational, written communication, verbal communication, problem-solving, and prioritization skills

Experience supporting client audits, regulatory inspections, or quality system assessments

Other duties may be assigned as needed

Element is one of the fastest growing testing, inspection and certification businesses in the world. Globally we have more than 9,000 brilliant minds operating from 270 sites across 30 countries. Together we share an ambitious purpose to ‘Make tomorrow safer than today’.

jobs.title: Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pattern Energy is a leading renewable energy company that develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind and solar generation, transmission, and energy storage facilities. Our mission is to transition the world to renewable energy through the sustainable development and responsible operation of facilities with respect for the environment, communities, and cultures where we have a presence.

Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises.

Pattern Energy operates in the United States and Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Houston, San Diego, New York and Toronto. Pattern Energy Group's corporate headquarters are in San Francisco. Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 35 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers.

Responsibilities

JOB PURPOSE

The Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, EPC is responsible for ensuring environmental compliance and supporting strategic risk planning for Pattern’s projects during execution, with a primary focus on wind, transmission, and solar energy projects in the United States and Canada, and ancillary support for compliance efforts in other jurisdictions as needed.

This role leads and coordinates environmental construction permit compliance activities, supports environmental compliance programs and tools, and works closely with internal project teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups to ensure Pattern’s projects meet applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements.

To support ongoing Pattern projects, viable candidates may also be considered if they live near Pattern project locations in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Montana, North Dakota, or New Mexico, as an optional work location arrangement.

Key Accountabilities

The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following:

Lead environmental construction permit compliance activities in coordination with Pattern EPC group managers, engineering and construction managers, project construction contractors, and Pattern Environmental Development and Operations teams.
Manage and coordinate project environmental personnel, including environmental consultants, EPC and specialty contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups as appropriate.
Conduct environmental compliance reviews, participate in monthly management meetings, complete site audits, and support compliance root-cause analysis investigations and reviews.
Assist in the development and implementation of Pattern environmental compliance programs, procedures, and project execution documents.
Create, maintain, and update project environmental compliance matrices during project execution.
Develop and deliver Environmental Awareness Training for EPC and contractor staff.
Coordinate with federal, state, provincial, and local environmental agency leads to resolve environmental concerns during construction.
Budget for and manage consultants providing project-level environmental support services, including construction environmental monitoring and wildlife mitigation strategies.
Represent Pattern in industry organizations and technical committees, supporting benchmarking, collaboration, and thought leadership across the renewable energy sector.

Qualifications

Experience/Qualifications/Education Required

Educational Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a science-oriented field such as Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences, Wildlife, or a related field is required. An advanced degree in Law, Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a comparable discipline is preferred.

Required Work Experience

The following criteria will be used as a basis for Pattern to select a qualified applicant:

Seven or more years of experience in environmental, natural resources, or energy-related projects, preferably in renewable energy.
Experience with wind, transmission, and/or solar power permitting, environmental construction compliance, and environmental fieldwork.
Familiarity with federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations related to stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, wildlife, archaeology, environmental due diligence, and associated compliance programs.
Extensive experience with stormwater best management practices, including design, implementation, maintenance, and cost considerations.
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams and managing environmental consultants and contractors.

Additional Requirements

Must possess strengths in the following:

Strong time management, diplomacy, and specialized environmental compliance knowledge.
Ability to make informed recommendations regarding the interpretation and application of environmental permits, regulations, and laws in evolving regulatory environments.
Ability to analyze, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources and translate findings into clear written deliverables.
Strong professional communication skills, including the ability to influence best practices and change within projects and the broader organization.
Ability to multi-task, adapt quickly, work well under pressure, collaborate in large teams and one-on-one settings, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to approximately 25%, depending on project needs.

Technical Skills

Computer skills – working knowledge of Windows-based business software applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Environmental compliance – detailed knowledge of environmental regulatory frameworks, including wildlife, natural resources, stormwater, site restoration, spills, waste, audits, and project-specific permit or regulatory requirements for projects in the United States and/or Canada.

The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses.

**Environmental Research Group, LLC (ERG)** is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our Environmental Compliance Team to support a variety of environmental compliance projects. When not performing work at various project sites, this position can be based anywhere in the USA with preference given to candidates that reside within an hour commute of a regional or international airport.


The Environmental Scientist is expected to support and lead a variety of projects, working both independently and as part of a team. An experienced multi\-disciplinary background is valued for this position. You will plan and execute technical projects, conduct regulatory research, write reports, support permitting process, conduct site visits and surveys, and collaborate with a team, while remaining flexible to prioritize clients' needs and deadlines.


This position requires traveling on average one week per month for fieldwork and site visits, with durations of 3 to 14 days on site. Some international travel would be required with this position. The field work can include working indoors, outdoors, and/or industrial locations, and wearing Level D Personal Protective Equipment.


Founded in 2000, ERG provides environmental compliance, natural resources, and cultural resources consulting services. We are a value\-driven, employee\-first, government small business contractor. Trust, expertise, and compassion drive our success, while gratitude, joy, and adaptability drive the team.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a closely related field. Master's degree, Professional Engineer, and/or relevant certifications are a plus.
* Working knowledge of federal environmental programs. Knowledge and experience with Department of War (DoW) environmental policy is a plus.
* Excellent interpersonal communication, writing skills, and attention to detail.
* Ability to work independently, manage time efficiently, and be responsive.
* Flexibility to serve in multiple roles and teams depending on the client and project.
* Must be able to pass DoW security clearances and background checks and obtain a passport.
* US citizenship required.

**Knowledge and Experience**

* The position requires experience with multiple federal and state environmental regulatory areas, with a focus in one or more programs including but not limited to environmental compliance auditing and inspections; Environmental Management System; solid waste, toxic substances, spill response, stormwater, wastewater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, storage tanks, air quality, and/or resilience.
* Experience with environmental auditing and public involvement are a plus.
* Experience in preparing and writing environmental plans, permits, and reports, and conducting environmental audits to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local requirements.
* Experience in providing environmental project support to clients, including conducting site visits as needed. Work experience with federal government agencies, DoW, and state environmental agencies.
* Relevant environmental and technical certifications and trainings are a plus.


The annual salary range for this position is $80,000\-$90,000, commensurate with experience, and bonuses are offered for exceptional performance. ERG is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Disability and Veteran statuses. ERG also participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's E\-Verify Program to ensure that all employees hired are legally able to work in the United States.

jobs.company: South Coast Air Quality Management District
jobs.title: Principal Air Quality Chemist
jobs.description:
South Coast Aqmd And Job Overview

ABOUT SOUTH COAST AQMD

South Coast Air Quality Management District (South Coast AQMD) is one of the largest and most technologically sophisticated environmental regulatory agencies in the nation, serving a four-county region that includes Los Angeles, Orange County, Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and the Coachella Valley. South Coast AQMD's headquarters is located in Diamond Bar, 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, at the junction of the 57 and 60 Freeways. With a highly diverse "Clean Air Team" of over 870 employees, an annual budget of $225.2 million, and a state-of-the art air quality laboratory, our mission is to ensure clean air and a healthy environment. South Coast AQMD is an organization you can be proud to work for -- we make a difference in the quality of life in Southern California!

South Coast AQMD is committed to creating and maintaining a work environment that appreciates the unique backgrounds, skills, and experiences of our employees and fosters professional development and growth. South Coast AQMD respects the ideas and perspectives of our stakeholders and works to bring them together toward the common goal of clean air.

About Our Laboratory

South Coast AQMD's laboratory employs over 40 staff in a 20,000 square foot state-of-the-art facility dedicated to air quality sample analysis. It provides a broad array of services generating actionable data that is used for strategic planning, investigating complaints from the community, evaluating new products and processes, supporting incident responses and determining compliance with regulations. We also provide data to the California Air Resources Board, US EPA, law enforcement agencies, and universities. Results generated by the laboratory have been the catalyst for agency-wide policy decisions, special studies, and technology development. We analyze over 60,000 samples per year using various analytical laboratory techniques; including GC, IC, LC, GC-MS, XRF, XRD, FTIR, microscopic analysis, ICP-MS, and PTR-MS to generate detailed information on the types and amount of pollutants in ambient air. The South Coast AQMD laboratory is at the forefront of method development for ambient air analyses and obtains national recognition in the field of air quality analytical chemistry.

About This Position

The South Coast AQMD is seeking qualified candidates to fill a Principal Air Quality Chemist vacancy. From this recruitment process, we expect to establish an eligible list from which current and future vacancies may be filled, during the 6–12-month life of the list.

Principal Chemists are expected to have expertise in many analytical techniques, data analysis, and to supervise the work of staff in their respective group. Therefore, the most competitive candidates for this position will bring a strong combination of education, atmospheric and analytical chemistry training and experience, broad knowledge of QA/QC procedures, and supervisory skills and readiness. This position will be responsible for oversight of the South Coast AQMD laboratory's Advanced Spectrometry and Microscopy groups. The primary role of the Advanced Spectrometry Principal Chemist is to help with community monitoring needs under several South Coast AQMD programs, including AB 617 (Community Air Toxics Monitoring), incident response, rule development and support, and special monitoring projects using a mobile Proton-Transfer-Reaction-Time-of-Flight-Mass Spectrometer (PTR-MS) and other advanced instrumentation.

The Principal Air Quality Chemist is a supervisory position reporting to the Laboratory Manager. This vacant position is one of four Principal positions making up the laboratory supervisory team; each team consists of eight to sixteen chemists, technicians, and support staff. Teams are aligned by function, including compliance analysis, ambient VOC/toxics analysis, aerosol analysis, and advanced spectrometry/microscopy.

EXAMPLE OF DUTIES

The general Example of Duties for this classification are highlighted below, for full description of duties please refer to this link here .

Plans, organizes, and supervises the work of staff assigned to a laboratory section involved in qualitative and quantitative analyses to isolate, identify, and quantify air contaminants; reviews requests for analyses, determines the level of difficulty, and assigns work; and provides technical and administrative guidance to professional and technical staff and evaluates performance.
Develops, supervises, prioritizes, and evaluates programs and projects; maintains workload statistics on unit activities; prepares program- and activity-related reports and analyses; reviews and edits technical reports prepared by laboratory staff to ensure accuracy of data, appropriateness of methodologies, and soundness of findings and conclusions; and identifies and maintains data quality objectives on a program basis.
Serves as a technical expert and resource for South Coast AQMD staff regarding chemistry-related air quality matters and on a variety of technical advisory committees; maintains a broad understanding of current research into causes, sources, and chemical reactions contributing to air quality problems; and consults with outside experts regarding air quality issues relevant to laboratory programs and projects.
Applies professional training and experience and keeps abreast of updated and new chemical laboratory methods, instrumentation, protocols, and practices through review of professional literature and other research resources and evaluates staff recommendations to ensure the laboratory uses the most effective and up-to-date techniques in analyzing air contaminants, accomplishing the work of the unit, and meeting new or changing South Coast AQMD rules.
Reviews and approves test methods used by private laboratories for compliance with South Coast AQMD rules.
Represents South Coast AQMD at scientific conferences and prepares for publication and presents research reports and papers on methods, procedures, results, and conclusions relating to laboratory analyses.
Testifies in court and before public bodies and hearing boards.
Prepares annual budget request for the section and submits written justification for budget items requested; and is responsible for the preparation of grant proposals for federal government or other funding.
Acts for the laboratory services manager, as needed.

Desirable Qualifications

MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

In addition to the Minimum Qualifications which follow, the most competitive candidates will also possess:

Experience with the measurement of Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in ambient air, and the analysis, interpretation, and presentation of resultant data sets.
Experience with mobile measurements and/or field studies using research grade instrumentation, particularly mass spectrometry techniques such as PTR-MS and spectroscopic methods such as CRDS and TILDAS; along with other analytical techniques for the measurement of ambient gases and particles.
Experience with microscopic analysis for asbestos and other ambient particulate matter using polarized light microscopy, electron microscopy with EDS, XRD, FTIR, and other techniques.
Knowledge of QA/QC procedures and guidelines to ensure data is accurate and representative of the samples being collected following proper documentation procedures.
Detailed knowledge of matters directly related to ambient air analysis, laboratory instrumentation and data management.
Exceptional leadership, oral presentation, and written communication skills.
Experience overseeing the work of laboratory professionals and support staff.
Ability to identify and resolve complex programmatic and administrative challenges in a fair, impartial, and professional manner.
Ability to implement and track the progress of programs and innovative solutions to improve efficiency and productivity.
Ability to conceptualize mobile monitoring and field data using GIS based visualizations.
Ability to manage workloads to ensure timely turnaround of sample analysis and data collected during field measurements.
Ability to lead teams operating field instrumentation, both stationary and mobile, that is used extensively for monitoring pollutants near facilities and in nearby communities as well as for incident response.
Ability to oversee contracts for monitoring studies along with collaborating with researchers at universities and other agencies.
Ability to present technical data to various stakeholders having a wide range of scientific and professional backgrounds.
Strong computer and data review skills for large complex datasets that harmonize data from several instruments often with different time resolutions.
Flexibility, dependability, and a positive, can-do attitude.

Minimum Qualifications

EDUCATION:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, preferably with an emphasis in qualitative and quantitative analysis.

Experience

One (1) year as a Senior Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (One year working as a Manager, Supervisor, Senior Chemist, or similar leadership position that oversees a group of chemists focused on air quality measurements and/or research) OR
Three (3) years as an Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (Three years working as a Chemist conducting air quality analysis).

KNOWLEDGE OF:
Current methods, procedures, protocols, and instrumentation relating to organic, inorganic, and physical qualitative and quantitative analysis; operational principles of relevant chemical laboratory instrumentation and techniques; principles and practices of project management, supervision, training, and budgeting; relevant professional research literature and resources; principles and methods of statistical analysis; working knowledge of database design, information management, and computer programming, as they relate to laboratory analysis of air contaminants; safety procedures and practices relating to laboratory work; PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; professional report writing; South Coast AQMD rules and federal and State laws related to chemical analysis of air contaminants; and protocols and standards for laboratory analysis of air quality samples.

SKILL OR ABILITY TO:
Supervise, evaluate, train, and assign work to professional and technical staff involved in routine and complex qualitative and quantitative organic, inorganic and physical analysis of air quality samples; effectively use available resources in planning and organizing programs and projects; evaluate the effectiveness of programs and projects in meeting laboratory and overall South Coast AQMD objectives; oversee the development and implementation of new laboratory methods, procedures, and protocols, the adaptation of existing instrumentation and methods for new purposes, and the evaluation of new instrumentation; understand and interpret applicable laws, rules, and regulations; edit and write detailed, accurate reports on laboratory projects, analyses, methodologies, findings, and conclusions; prepare funding proposals; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; proficiently use PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.

LICENSE:
Possession of a valid California Class "C" Driver's License and a good driving record may be required.

Other Important Information

APPLICATION PACKETS MUST INCLUDE

A completed employment application covering at least the past 10 years of employment history (or longer if you have other relevant experience), and your entire South Coast AQMD employment history if you are a South Coast AQMD employee.

Our Commitment To Equity, Diversity, And Inclusion

California State University (CSU), Chico is a comprehensive and residential public university, holding Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) designation. Chico State operates as part of the 22-campus CSU system, which educates the most ethnically, economically, and academically diverse student body in the nation. The University enrolls over 14,000 students, with over half identifying as first-generation college students.

Chico State is committed to recruiting outstanding candidates. The ideal candidate will embrace our values predicated on the primacy of student success and the elimination of equity gaps, have demonstrated experience working with diverse populations, and will contribute to policies, programs, and practices that support an inclusive, accessible, and equitable learning and working environment.

Earth and Environmental Sciences

Position Summary

The Earth and Environmental Sciences Department in the College of Natural Sciences is collecting application materials for a pool of lecturers with positions available as determined by need during the 2026-27 academic year. Appointments from the lecturer pool are temporary and often made just prior to the start of the academic term.

Minimum Qualifications

The minimum education requirement for a lecturer appointment is a Master’s of Science in Environmental Science, Geology, Earth Science, or related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with teaching experience and with a Ph.D. in Environmental Science, Geology, Earth Science, or related field will be given preference.

Responsibilities

Lecturer positions in the department carry responsibilities in the areas of teaching, grading, syllabus and course development. Teaching assignments are based upon qualifications of the individual and the needs of the department.

How To Apply

Applicants must provide a current cover letter (including how you have addressed, or plan to address teaching to diverse student groups), a CV, a list of courses you believe you are qualified to teach and for which you wish to be considered, a copy of unofficial transcripts for your highest earned degree, and contact information of three professional references. Additional information may be requested at a later time. All applicants must apply online, applications submitted via email or in-person to the department will not be considered. For information about specific courses offered, please refer to the University Catalog .

The Department

The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences offers B.S. degrees in Geology and Environmental Sciences as well as M.S. degrees in Environmental Sciences and Geosciences. The Department continues to grow and currently serves over 160 majors and over 15 graduate students. Faculty and students are actively involved in internal and external research grants and service contracts, and the University and College offer funding to support development of innovative student-learning techniques for both field and in-class activities. The Department is interdisciplinary with faculty having expertise and research interests in the areas of applied ecology, hydrology, biogeochemistry, atmospheric science, sedimentology, volcanology, paleontology, petrology, and oceanography. The Department houses a variety of research-grade instruments and computer resources available to both faculty and students as many of our students regularly present their research at national and international conferences. Water is a critical resource both locally and regionally and our department’s involvement with local water agencies, the CSU, Chico’s Center for Water and the Environment, as well various campus sustainability groups reflect our commitment to be leaders in water-related issues. More information may be viewed at http://www.csuchico.edu/erth/index.shtml .

Dr. Russell Shapiro, Search Committee Chair

400 W. 1st St., Chico, CA 95929-0205

rsshapiro@csuchico.edu

The person also will have a duty to report to the campus Title IX coordinator information pertaining to discrimination, harassment, sexual misconduct or exploitation, dating or domestic violence, stalking, and/or retaliation under CSU policy.

If you are a CalPERS retiree and have any questions regarding your work eligibility, reach out to Faculty Affairs via email ( facultyaffairs@csuchico.edu ) or phone (530-898-5029).

Graduate and undergraduate programs boast high-quality research experiences, exceptional faculty mentoring, and civic and global engagement opportunities. The campus motto, “Today Decides Tomorrow,” is brought to life by inclusive pedagogy, experiential learning, and co-curricular programming. Together, they will become leaders solving the challenges of the 21st century.

We acknowledge and are mindful that Chico State stands on lands that were originally occupied by the first people of this area, the Mechoopda, and we recognize their distinctive spiritual relationship with this land, the flora, the fauna, and the waters that run through campus.
