The Supervisor, Analytical Laboratory oversees daily operations and performance of analytical laboratory processes utilizing immunoassay and/or LC-MS/MS technology. This role ensures high-quality testing, regulatory compliance, and effective supervision of laboratory personnel while supporting ongoing process improvements and technical development initiatives.

Responsibilities

Laboratory Operations & Oversight

Provides day-to-day supervision of testing personnel and oversees reporting of laboratory test results for all CLIA-regulated methods.
Maintains required supervisory presence and accessibility through on-site, telephone, or electronic consultation.
Ensures laboratory operations comply with state and federal regulations, including CLIA General Supervisor responsibilities.
Monitors analytical performance, specimen examination, and adherence to established quality standards for immunoassay and/or LC-MS/MS workflows.
Identifies and resolves technical issues, working closely with laboratory leadership as needed.

Quality, Compliance & Documentation

Ensures Laboratory Occurrence Management (LOM) forms and corrective actions are completed accurately.
Participates in internal audits and proficiency testing.
Oversees and assists with preventive maintenance and calibration of laboratory instruments; coordinates with vendors for repairs or troubleshooting.
Develops, writes, and maintains Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and departmental forms.
Ensures adherence to Quality Assurance, HIPAA, confidentiality, safety regulations, and cybersecurity standards.

Staff Leadership & Development

Provides direct supervision and training for Laboratory Technicians and Assistants in accordance with regulatory requirements.
Conducts performance evaluations for direct reports.
Oversees onboarding, competency assessments, and orientation of laboratory personnel.
Supports continuing education requirements and fosters a culture of professional development.

Technical Expertise & Process Improvement

Performs technical studies to validate or improve clinical testing methods.
Collaborates with vendors on instrument validations and new technology implementations.
Assists with advanced troubleshooting involving equipment, instruments, and assay performance.
Participates in initiatives related to quality, safety, workflow efficiency, and document management.

Additional Responsibilities

Ensures prompt implementation of remedial actions when test systems deviate from performance specifications.
Maintains awareness of evolving laboratory needs and supports organizational goals with flexibility.
Performs additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education & Licensure

Bachelor’s degree in chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science (required).
Current California CLS license (Generalist, Toxicologist Scientist, or Clinical Chemist Scientist).
Out-of-state Medical Technologists may be considered if able to obtain a California CLS license within six months of hire.

Experience

Bachelor’s degree with 3+ years of CLS Leadership experience, or

Master’s degree with 2+ years of CLS Leadership experience, or

Minimum 2 years of experience after obtaining CLS/MT licensure.
Supervisory experience strongly preferred.

Technical & Professional Skills

Knowledgeable in clinical laboratory testing methods, techniques, equipment, and supplies.
Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills at all organizational levels.
High attention to detail and accuracy.
Demonstrated ability to lead staff and manage projects effectively.
Must meet continuing education requirements per California Department of Health Services.

Physical Requirements

Sitting: 50%
Walking: 30%
Standing: 20%
Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
Ability to read/interpret SOPs and convert instructions into daily tasks

Benefits

Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability Insurance
401(k) with Company Match
Paid Time Off and Holidays
Tuition Assistance
Behavioral and Health Care Resources

Must be a U.S Citizen, not offering sponsorship at this time

### **Job Description and Duties**


**Please note, the Water Boards do not participate in E\-Verify.**


Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to work in a high\-profile position to help California communities address water quality issues? Do you enjoy a fast\-paced environment with opportunities to innovate and lead positive change? If so, then this is the position for you! Apply today and join our dedicated and driven team.


The State Water Resource Control Board’s Division of Financial Assistance has two openings for an Environmental Scientist in the Loans and Grant Branch, Environmental Section, located at 1001 I Street, 16th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814\.


**Duties:**


Under the close supervision of a Senior Environmental Scientist, the Environmental Scientist is expected to:


Prepare, review and process environmental documents (i.e., Notice of Exemptions, Initial Studies, Negative or Mitigated Negative Declarations, Environmental Impact Reports, and associated mitigation monitoring measures) for Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds (SRF) projects and other funding projects, when the State Water Board is lead or responsible agency under California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Conduct site visits/inspections throughout the State to evaluate projects’ significant environmental impacts, confirm compliance with environmental conditions and attend public hearings as necessary.Coordinate, research, and analyze environmental data used in the preparation of biological reports and environmental documents. Ensure funding projects meet the CEQA, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and other federal environmental cross\-cutting requirements.Coordinate with federal, state, and local governmental agencies to determine the need for additional studies and/or mitigation measures to ensure compliance with CEQA and/or associated federal environmental laws/authorities and initiate consultation if necessary.
  

  

Work with environmental consultants and applicants to coordinate the preparation and review of CEQA notices, Initial Studies and Negative and Mitigated Negative Declarations, as appropriate, when the State Water Board is the CEQA lead agency; and file Notices of Exemption, Notices of Completion, and Notices of Determination with the Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation, State Clearinghouse.Attend project meetings and provide environmental information and guidance to State Water Board staff and project applicants. Prepare Board Items, make presentations or briefings to the State Water Board members. Review and comment on draft environmental documents prepared for SRF projects, and water supply permits to ensure compliance with the CEQA, NEPA and other federal environmental cross\-cutting laws/authorities. Work cooperatively with stakeholders (general public, federal, state and local government agencies, tribes and other interested parties) and participate in stakeholder meetings. Develop environmental review clearances; perform field reviews and compliance inspections; and prepare project files and updated databases.

Candidates must possess essential personal qualifications including integrity, initiative, dependability, good judgment, the ability to work cooperatively with others, and the ability to perform the assigned duties of the class.

In accordance with the Statewide Telework Policy and GC 14200, the successful candidate must reside in California upon appointment. Proof of residency may be required.


Salary Information \- CalHR salary rules allow appointment at the entrance rate (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 2, § 599\.673\) of a classification. For classes with alternate ranges, placement is based on education/experience. Employees appointed to the Attorney or Water Resource Control Engineer classification will receive Recruitment Higher Above Minimum (HAM) rate in accordance with the approved Civil Service Pay Scales.

Position Summary

The Environmental Specialist is responsible for managing and executing multi-media environmental compliance programs
in a regulated aerospace manufacturing environment. This role requires hands-on ownership of air quality, hazardous waste, stormwater, and wastewater programs
in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations, with a strong emphasis on California-specific requirements
.

This position serves as the primary environmental subject matter expert
for the facility, ensuring compliance with agencies such as SCAQMD, DTSC, CUPA, LACSD and California Water Boards
. The Environmental Specialist will lead regulatory reporting, inspections, and audits, while partnering with operations, engineering, and leadership to maintain full environmental compliance and minimize risk.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory Compliance & Environmental Programs

Manage environmental compliance programs across air, hazardous waste, stormwater, and wastewater
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations (EPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, CUPA, LACSD, and Water Boards)
Interpret environmental permits and ensure adherence to permit conditions and regulatory requirements

Air Quality Compliance (SCAQMD)

Manage facility air permits and ensure compliance with permit conditions
Track emissions (VOC/HAP) and prepare annual emissions inventories/reporting (AER)
Evaluate process changes for regulatory applicability and compliance

Hazardous Waste Management (DTSC – Title 22)

Oversee hazardous waste programs including:
Coordinate hazardous waste disposal vendors and ensure regulatory compliance

CUPA / CERS Reporting

Manage Hazardous Materials Business Plans (HMBP) and chemical inventory reporting
Maintain compliance within the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS)
Aboveground storage tank (SPCC/APSA) requirements

Stormwater Compliance (IGP / SMARTS)

Develop and maintain the Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP)
Conduct stormwater inspections, sampling, and reporting
Ensure compliance with the California Industrial General Permit (IGP) via SMARTS

Industrial Wastewater Compliance (LA County Sanitation District – LACSD)

Support industrial wastewater permit compliance, including:

Audits, Inspections & Reporting

Conduct internal environmental audits and facility inspections
Lead and support regulatory inspections (AQMD, DTSC, CUPA, LACSD, and Water Boards)
Prepare and submit regulatory reports and maintain compliance documentation

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Investigate environmental incidents and compliance deviations
Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective/preventive actions (CAPA)
Identify opportunities for waste reduction, emissions reduction, and environmental performance improvement

Training & Cross-Functional Support

Develop and deliver environmental compliance training to site personnel
Partner with operations, maintenance, and engineering to support compliance initiatives
Serve as environmental SME for projects, process changes, and new equipment

Required Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or related field

Experience

3–7+ years of environmental compliance experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or industrial environments
Demonstrated experience managing multi-media environmental programs (air, waste, water)
Direct experience with California environmental regulations, including:

Technical Expertise

Experience preparing and submitting environmental reports:
Knowledge of:
Ability to interpret regulatory requirements, permits, and compliance obligations

Operational Skills

Experience supporting or leading environmental audits and regulatory inspections
Strong documentation, organization, and data tracking skills
Proficiency with Excel and environmental reporting systems

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in aerospace, coatings, metal finishing, or chemical manufacturing environments
Familiarity with:
Experience with:
Professional certifications (preferred but not required):

What Success Looks Like In This Role

Ability to independently manage environmental compliance programs with minimal oversight
Confidence interacting directly with regulatory agencies and leading inspections
Strong understanding of California environmental regulations and reporting systems
Proactive identification and mitigation of compliance risks
Effective partnership with operations to maintain compliance without disrupting production

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment.

jobs.description:
There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.


**Who are we looking for?**

We’re looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist to join WA \- **Environmental Impact Assessment** team.


Our WA \- **Environmental Impact Assessment** business has maintained strong growth in recent years and is currently one of the largest groups in WA, being a leader in impact assessment and approvals, terrestrial ecology, and marine. Our diverse team contributes to a wide variety of projects, with a strategic focus on renewable energy, critical minerals and Defence at a regional, national and global scale.


At GHD, we understand the importance of maintaining a healthy work\-life balance. That’s why we offer flexible working arrangements tailored to support your lifestyle and commitments. This role is open to both **full\-time** and **part\-time hours** , with a minimum of 20 hours per week, providing you the flexibility to thrive professionally while balancing your personal life. Join us in an environment that truly values your well\-being as much as your expertise.


Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.


Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.


**Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:**

* Conduct comprehensive environmental assessments and impact studies in compliance with Australian regulatory frameworks.
* Lead and contribute to the preparation of high\-quality proposals and client\-ready technical reports following relevant standards and guidelines, client requirements, and GHD project guidelines.
* Act as a Project Manager for routine projects, collaborating effectively with project stakeholders to ensure successful client experience in project delivery.
* Supervise the daily activities of a project or design team including allocating and checking work and providing feedback on performance.
* Marketing including the development and submission of proposals for routine, low risk projects which at times may involve convincing internal and external stakeholders.
* Communicate with clients about current work and future needs, provide timely updates on project progress.
Supervise, support and train less experienced members of the team.  
* 

**What you will bring to the team:**

* Bachelor of Science (Environmental) degree or related field.
* 5\+ years’ relevant experience, with sound knowledge of Commonwealth, State and Local Government environmental regulatory requirements.
* Applies broad knowledge of a professional discipline or advanced knowledge of technical practices demonstrated in a relevant industry or consulting business.
* A track record for delivering exceptional client experience, and an eye for business development opportunities.
* Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with diverse stakeholders.
* Strong numerical, analytical, and writing skills, including experience in the preparation of reports for clients and or regulators.
* Current C class drivers’ licence
Proficient in Microsoft 365 suite (excel, word, outlook)  
*

**Ph \+61 8 6222 8631**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. "At Caltrans, we foster a supportive environment that encourages open communication and mutual respect, empowering you to bring your best ideas forward. Our commitment to work-life balance ensures you have time to recharge and pursue personal passions, while our dedication to job security guarantees a stable and fulfilling career."

About the Position:

The Caltrans Environmental Scientist performs a broad range of work concerning environmental issues related to protecting California's resources as related to transportation projects. Incumbents do field analyses; prepare environmental documents and technical studies, environmental permitting packages and regulatory permits; ensure compliance with various environmental laws and regulations; and conduct environmental protection, planning, and mitigation activities. Incumbents apply scientific methods and principles to analyze and evaluate available data on the effects of transportation projects on all aspects of the environment; prepare and review CEQA/NEPA and other technical documents to determine the effects; and implement mitigation strategies to lessen the impact of those projects. Under the general direction of the Environmental Branch Chief, the incumbent is an interdisciplinary team member who must establish and maintain a professional working relationship with internal project delivery partners, various regulatory agencies, local partners and interested parties involved with Caltrans' projects. The incumbent must be solution oriented and will need to investigate innovative solutions to meet deliverables. This work requires strong oral and written skills with the specific ability to prepare technical reports as well as written and verbal correspondence. This position may require site visits, sometimes to remote areas, which may require driving a personal or state vehicle on public roadways or on uneven terrain.

Welcome to Verdantas, where innovation meets sustainability, and your career finds purpose!

At Verdantas, we’re redefining environmental consulting and sustainable engineering through our use of cutting-edge modeling and digital technology and our genuine commitment to people. Our work spans high-growth sectors like water resources, resilient land use, energy transformation, and civil infrastructure.

Our commitment to excellence, across more than 90 offices, is championed by a team of over 2,000 experts, scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists, embedded in a people-focused culture, prioritizing the well-being of our employees, clients, and the communities we serve. We partner with clients to deliver smart, data-driven solutions to complex environmental and infrastructure challenges. We don’t just solve problems; we help shape a more sustainable future.

Join a people-first culture that values your well-being, empowers your growth, and amplifies your impact. At Verdantas, your career goes beyond the expected, and your work helps build a better world.

Ready to shape the future of resilient communities?

We are looking for motivated Environmental Scientist/Qualified SWPPP Practitioner
(QSP) to join our team! This is a mid-level stormwater professional position, depending on experience. This role will be a great fit for you if you’re ready to learn and grow in your new career, are seeking a collaborative work environment, and are passionate about the environment. This position is remote
, but must be local to Santa Rosa, Sacramento, Fresno, San Ramon, or Marysville, CA.

In this role, you’ll support environmental and stormwater compliance projects, including assisting clients in complying with stormwater regulations and preventing pollutants from leaving the project boundary and entering our waterways. Responsibilities will include conducting stormwater inspections, developing and implementing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and/or site stabilization plans, conducting stormwater sampling, conducting desktop evaluations, providing on-site training to construction crews, and preparing related documentation and reporting.

Depending on qualifications and experience, this position generally performs work under the supervision/guidance of more senior staff supporting both routine and complex projects. This position may support assigned initiatives and special projects. Travel and overnight travel will be required, with periodic weekend and overtime work.

What You'll Do:

Cross-training in natural resources, including wetlands and/or environmental permitting
Knowledge of water quality or Stormwater management information, techniques, practices, laws, and regulations of the job or occupational field
Knowledge of the California State Water Board Permits
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation

What You'll Bring:

BS or BA degree, preferably in an environmental discipline, sciences, or engineering
Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience supporting experience in SWPPP, including sampling and analysis, non-storm water and storm water visual observations, and preparation of Rain Event Action Plans, environmental restoration, landscape construction, and erosion control
Current QSP Certification (QSD Certification is preferred)
Experience with the California Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS)
Familiarity with the California Stormwater Construction General Permit and the California Stormwater Quality Association (CASQA) Construction Handbook
Possess knowledge of environmental key issues and trends, including emerging best practices and technology, and familiar with industry language and terminology
Competency with Google Earth KMZ

jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, US
jobs.description:
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is seeking a motivated **Student Assistant, Environmental Compliance** to join the **Environmental Services Group (ESG)** within the **Environment, Waste \& Radiation Protection Division**. This is an exciting opportunity to gain real\-world experience supporting environmental compliance and monitoring programs at a world\-renowned national laboratory.

  



As a Student Assistant, you'll work alongside environmental professionals on meaningful projects that help protect people and the environment. You'll gain hands\-on experience conducting compliance assessments and inspections, participating in environmental sampling and monitoring, collecting and analyzing data, preparing reports and procedures, and supporting a variety of environmental programs.

  



Whether you're exploring a career in environmental science, environmental engineering, sustainability, or Environment, Health \& Safety (EHS), this position provides valuable experience, professional mentorship, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while building your resume.

  



**You will:**


* Assist in data collection and provide support for environmental compliance programs, including but not limited to, air quality, hazardous materials management, sanitary sewer, and surface water quality.
* Assist in preparing regulatory reports including analyzing and summarizing data, writing, editing and QA/QC.
* Assist with inspections and compliance assessments: collect and maintain inspection records, enter inspection data into various software systems, submit maintenance requests and complete basic stormwater and hazardous material storage inspections.
* Prepare and maintain spreadsheets to track compliance data.
* Assist with collection of environmental samples under direct supervision of EH\&S specialists or technicians.
* Consolidate, review and edit internal documents including procedures and work instructions.
* Perform data entry, spreadsheet manipulation and preparing presentation materials.

  

**We are looking for:**


* A full time student in at least their Junior year working toward an undergraduate or graduate degree in Environmental Science, Health or Engineering or similar technical degree.
* Familiarity with environmental laws and regulations and technical aspects of environmental science.
* Ability to demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to enter and manage data in various software systems and prepare graphical presentations.

  

**Additional information:**


* **Application date:** Priority consideration will be given to candidates who apply by **August 5, 2026**. Applications will be accepted until the job posting is removed.
* **Appointment type:** This is a variable 1 year, student assistant appointment with the possibility of renewal based upon satisfactory job performance, continuing availability of funds and ongoing operational needs. The incumbent will work approximately 12 hours per week during the school year and up to 20 hours per week during the summer.
* **Salary range:** The hourly range for this position is $21\.40 \- $50\.20\. Pay will be dependent on the current level of education.
* **Background check:** This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
* **Work modality:** Work will be primarily performed at:Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA with occasional telework for data\-entry projects. A REAL ID or other acceptable form of identification is required to access Berkeley Lab sites (for more information ).
* **Work authorization:** Candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

  

**Want to learn more about working at Berkeley Lab? Please visit:** **careers.lbl.gov**

  



Equal Employment Opportunity Employer: The foundation of Berkeley Lab is our Stewardship Values: Team Science, Service, Trust, Innovation, and Respect; and we strive to build community with these shared values and commitments. Berkeley Lab is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We heartily welcome applications from all who could contribute to the Lab's mission of leading scientific discovery, excellence, and professionalism. In support of our rich global community, all qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, or other protected categories under State and Federal law.

jobs.title: Construction Inspector - Water Resources
jobs.description:
BKF is hiring a Construction Inspector
to execute onsite construction inspections to ensure the project is being constructed in compliance with the contract requirements and applicable permits.

Responsibilities:

General

Inspect a variety of construction including but not limited to repair of pipelines, water mains, sewers, lift stations, and treatment plants
Advises Resident Engineer or Agency Project Manager and informs contractors of any variances from approved plans and specifications
Takes samples of materials, prepares test specimens, and assist in conducting field tests, or refers samples for laboratory analysis
Checks the location of public utilities to avoid interference with construction work
Assists PM in review of project submittals, RFI's, and CCO's
Verifies acceptability of material incorporated into the project by Certificates of Compliance, shop drawings, and test reports
Maintains material and inspection records
Maintains a daily diary, photo log, contract item quantities
Other duties as assigned

Water and Wastewater infrastructure

Verify the installation and proper sealing of water pipelines, ensuring no leaks or contamination
Oversee the construction and retrofitting of stormwater, water, and wastewater treatment facilities
Ensure proper grading, drainage, and erosion control measures are in place to manage water flow and prevent pollution
Check for compliance with health and safety standards, especially related to water quality, drinking water safety, and wastewater discharge regulations
Monitor backflow prevention, cross-connection controls, and ensure plumbing systems meet sanitary standards
Test water pressure and flow in pipelines, and inspect valves, pumps, and treatment plant equipment
Oversee sewer line cleaning, pipe relining, and trenchless repair methods
Ensure that environmental impacts, such as erosion, sedimentation, and stormwater runoff, are mitigated

Environmental and Health Compliance

Inspect for compliance with the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, and other environmental regulations
Ensure proper handling, disposal, and treatment of wastewater to avoid pollution
Check stormwater systems to ensure they meet environmental protection requirements, including those related to wetlands and floodplains

Requirements

Minimum Education, Licensure, or Certification Required

College degree or min. 5 years' work experience in related field
Valid California Class C driver's license and an acceptable driver's record are required

Desired Certifications

Certified Public Infrastructure Inspector (CPII)
ICC Reinforced Concrete Inspection Certification
ICC Masonry Inspection Certification
ICC Welding Inspection Certification
ACI Concrete Field-Testing Technician - Grade 1 Certification
Qualified SWPPP Certification
Fall protection Safety Training
First Aid & CPR

Minimum Experience Required

2 + years of experience in the supervision or inspection of engineering construction work including reading and interpreting complex construction plans and specifications, OR
5 years' work experience in related trade/field

Desired Construction management Experience

We are seeking candidates with experience in some of the following areas. While not every item is required, experience in a combination of these areas will be highly valued:

Large diameter sewer and water pipeline, including trenchless installations
Water and wastewater treatment plants, including membrane filtration technology
Sewer lift stations
Booster pump stations
Groundwater wells
Stormwater diversion, capture, and treatment
Flood control infrastructure
SCADA installation, integration, and startup commissioning

Other Required Skills

Knowledgeable with construction methods and procedures, Caltrans and Greenbook standard plans and specifications
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Able to work well with other people, contractors, agency personnel, the public
Interacts well with other staff, public, government agencies
Able to effectively operate a computer and basic computer programs such as Word & Excel

The typical base salary range for this position is $120,640.00 - $156,000.00 annually, depending upon skills, experience, education, and geographical location, hourly wage
Competitive salaries, end of year bonuses, profit sharing, and 401k
BKF pays multiple of the premiums for medical, dental, and vision coverage and 50% for your dependents
Generous vacation and sick time packages
8 Paid Holidays
Flexible schedules
Education reimbursement, Paid annual dues for professional and societal organizations

### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Fisheries Branch is seeking motivated candidates for a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) position. This position serves as the subject matter expert and coordinator for efforts to incorporate Parentage\-Based Tagging (PBT) into existing or new salmonid monitoring programs and anadromous hatchery practices for the purposes of conservation, mitigation and enhancement of California’s salmon fisheries. The incumbent will provide coordination and expertise for developing, implementing and integrating PBT into anadromous hatchery practices, coordinating tissue sampling in recreational and commercial fisheries, escapement, and emigration monitoring surveys. Coordinate with internal programs, and state and federal partners, ensuring that monitoring activities are scientifically sound and aligned with management needs.  

  

  

The position will provide technical expertise to interagency workgroups, participate in evaluating hatchery release strategies and interpret and communicate genetic analyses for application in fisheries and hatchery management. The position oversees the development and management of long term genetic databases, working closely with IT staff and genetic laboratories to establish data sharing agreements and integrate data systems. Responsibilities include conducting data analyses, ensuring data quality, and preparing presentations, technical reports, and annual summaries. The incumbent may also contribute to peer reviewed publications.  

  

  

Candidates should demonstrate strong initiative, professionalism, and the ability to manage complex projects independently. Effective decision making skills, adaptability, and the ability to work productively with interdisciplinary teams and diverse stakeholders are essential. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are required, including the ability to convey technical information clearly and professionally.

Job Posting: SCE Supervisor



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-525662* 

SCE Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/4/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you ready to take on a challenge and lead a dynamic team working on high\-profile environmental projects? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is seeking a Limited Term Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) to oversee the Southern California Edison (SCE) workload in our Habitat Conservation Planning Program. If you are a self\-motivated individual who thrives in fast\-paced, complex work environments and is passionate about conservation and environmental protection, we want to hear from you!  

  

  

About the Role: This is a working supervisor position where you will supervise and conduct environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning functions for SCE projects. You will play a key role in ensuring compliance with the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) agreements, working to maintain a balance between environmental protection and project progress.  

  

  

CDFW may be serving as the Lead or Responsible Agency under CEQA in order to issue permits, in this role you will initiate, execute, and manage contracts with SCE, coordinate with consultants, and oversee the preparation of critical documents. You will guide and support the issuance of permits, ensure timely completion of environmental reviews, facilitate mitigation efforts, and assess the success of conservation measures across multiple regions.  

  

  

What You Will Do:
\- Lead a team of Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialists) in environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning for SCE projects.
\- Oversee the development and certification of CEQA documents for SCE's permits, including a Master Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) and possibly CESA incidental take permits for projects across Regions 4, 5, and 6\.
\- Coordinate with regional and statewide staff to ensure project goals are met on time and in compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
\- Provide leadership and mentorship to your team, fostering a collaborative environment and driving success in complex, multi\-regional projects.
  

What We Are Looking For: We need someone who can take on a challenge, manage multiple complex projects, and ensure deadlines are met while maintaining the highest standards of environmental stewardship. If you are a problem\-solver with strong leadership skills and a passion for conservation, this could be the perfect role for you!  

  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)/Exam Bulletin  

  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Orange/Santa Barbara/San Diego counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Field site visits will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear a uniform in accordance with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) during field surveys and public interactions, both within and outside the Region as directed by the supervisor. A valid driver's license is required travel and field site visits to remote or rural areas where alternative transportation is not feasible. Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

This person performs a variety of professional scientific office and field work primarily in the Southern Fisheries District comprised of Tulare, Kern, and Kings Counties, and assists the Inland Fisheries Unit Region\-wide. Incumbent independently performs fishery resource management analysis, research, surveys, investigations, and studies; writes final reports; prepares regulatory and compliance documents; prepares non\-routine correspondence and answers non\-routine questions from the public. Incumbent provides consultative advice to various governmental entities and agencies. Incumbent shares responsibility for the fishery on the Kern Plateau including Little Kern Golden trout, Kern River Rainbow trout, and California Golden trout.

You will guide and support the issuance of permits, ensure timely completion of environmental reviews, facilitate mitigation efforts, and assess the success of conservation measures across multiple regions.  

  

  

What You Will Do:
\- Lead a team of Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialists) in environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning for SCE projects.
\- Oversee the development and certification of CEQA documents for SCE's permits, including a Master Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) and possibly CESA incidental take permits for projects across Regions 4, 5, and 6\.
\- Coordinate with regional and statewide staff to ensure project goals are met on time and in compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
\- Provide leadership and mentorship to your team, fostering a collaborative environment and driving success in complex, multi\-regional projects.
  

What We Are Looking For: We need someone who can take on a challenge, manage multiple complex projects, and ensure deadlines are met while maintaining the highest standards of environmental stewardship. If you are a problem\-solver with strong leadership skills and a passion for conservation, this could be the perfect role for you!  

  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)/Exam Bulletin  

  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Orange/Santa Barbara/San Diego counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Field site visits will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear a uniform in accordance with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) during field surveys and public interactions, both within and outside the Region as directed by the supervisor. A valid driver's license is required travel and field site visits to remote or rural areas where alternative transportation is not feasible. Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is actively seeking a creative, highly talented Area Manager with a focus on Environmental Site Assessment and Remediation. Area Managers are responsible for overseeing the performance of a group of major programs and/or projects to assure the achievement of internal and client\-facing KPIs. The location of this position is based in California. The successful candidate will be expected to continue to be involved in and execute billable work.

***The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:***

**Project Delivery:**

* Drives program performance to meet and/or exceed client satisfaction and KPIs.
* Understands and drives business performance and the attainment and exceedance of internal KPIs.
* Interacts with business leadership on governance \& risk issues to ensure risk management triggers are identified and addressed proactively.
* Develops and formulates solutions to client problems/issues.
* Participates in project reviews of major program/project dashboards/deep dives to identify issues and improve performance.
* Works to drive faster adoption of digital tools.
* Actively integrates international Enterprise Capabilities into project delivery to meet business targets and works with business leadership to manage transitions.
* Continually develops ideas for program and process improvement.
* Is directly engaged and manages high\-quality client projects.

**People:**

* Actively shares people management responsibilities for approximately 50 department staff.
* Builds, maintains, and facilitates trusting relationships with key contacts across the depth and breadth of three multinational chemical company client organizations.
* Serves as a focal point for major issue resolution and provides rapid follow\-up to address concerns.
* Participates in feedback for Project Managers to assure client satisfaction and long\-term growth.
* Develops and implements succession plans for the team and advises on the recruiting of key people to serve client needs.
* Assures project delivery employees are trained and mentored with a long\-term goal of training new project managers.
* Coaches project managers and team members on understanding business performance and internal KPIs; implements processes with Project Managers.
* Evaluates individual performance of project managers within the department.

**Business Development:**

* Works collaboratively with Client Account Manager(s), Practice Area Leaders, and Business Line Leadership to grow profitable backlog and ensure financial success of their respective client program.
* Develops budgets that allow for business development portfolio management, tracking \& optimizing wins and bookings, and project oversight.
* Leads capture strategies for key pursuits and major projects within the department, ensures those strategies yield high capture rates, and grows the business and relevant technical capabilities.

**Operations:**

* Acts as a point of escalation for project issues and makes recommendations to improve performance. This may include addressing project resourcing gaps, supporting technical issues, resolving invoicing and cash collection challenges, addressing subconsultant and vendor concerns, etc.
* Drives consistent project management practices and procedures in alignment with AECOM Project Delivery System (PDS) and Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.
* Ensures accuracy of Workload Planning Tool output for the department.
* Maintains departmental compliance with West Region Environment Pricing guidance and DOA approval framework.
* Ensures the accuracy of the department’s Salesforce pipeline data and associated Detailed Forecast data and output reports.

  

**Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

* Bachelor's degree and 8 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
* Successful candidates will have to pass a background check and a motor vehicle records check.
* US citizenship or permanent residency is required. Sponsor ship at this time or in the future will not be offered for this role.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's Degree preferred.
* 15 years related experience.
* California Professional Geologist or Professional Engineer
* Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to clearly articulate messages to a variety of audiences.
* Ability to influence others and move toward a common vision or goal.
* Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations.
* Resilient and tenacious with a propensity to persevere.
* Must be a team player and able to work collaboratively with and through others.
* Acute business acumen and understanding of organizational issues and challenges
* Strong knowledge and track record in the environmental / remediation business inclusive of risk\-based strategic asset management and advocacy in multiple state jurisdictions working for an Environmental Consultant.

  

**Additional Information**

Job Description And Duties

This person performs a variety of professional scientific office and field work primarily in the Southern Fisheries District comprised of Tulare, Kern, and Kings Counties, and assists the Inland Fisheries Unit Region-wide. Incumbent independently performs fishery resource management analysis, research, surveys, investigations, and studies; writes final reports; prepares regulatory and compliance documents; prepares non-routine correspondence and answers non-routine questions from the public. Incumbent provides consultative advice to various governmental entities and agencies. Incumbent shares responsibility for the fishery on the Kern Plateau including Little Kern Golden trout, Kern River Rainbow trout, and California Golden trout.

The South District staff lead conduct fishery studies, fish rescues, fish die-off investigations, fish population surveys (i.e. visual, e-fishing, snorkeling, and/or red surveys), exotic fish species and/or aquatic invasive species removals, water quantity/quality measurements, and site visits to evaluate site specific habitat conditions. Department Website: http://www.arb.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

We are seeking a dynamic and a driven leader in Riverside or Sacramento.

The California Air Resources Board’s (CARB) Office of Community Air Protection (OCAP) is seeking a highly capable and forward-looking Staff Air Pollution Specialist to join the Program Assessment and Reporting Section and help guide California’s community focused air quality work. This position offers a unique opportunity to apply advanced technical expertise and provide leadership in a program that plays a central role in supporting environmental equity across the state.

The successful candidate will bring strong analytical judgment, scientific insight, and strategic thinking to assist Section-level planning and decision making. This includes contributing to the development of Section and assisting achieve its strategic goals, supporting alignment across internal teams, and helping shape approaches that strengthen Program's effectiveness statewide.

Technical leadership is a key component of this role. The incumbent will draw on a deep understanding of air quality science and community level exposure assessment to support the development and refinement of analytical approaches used across the program. This includes interpreting diverse technical information, synthesizing complex findings, and helping ensure that analyses are clearly communicated to both technical and non-technical audiences.

The position also involves providing leadership in collaborative efforts with community partners, local agencies, and internal CARB divisions. By fostering strong communication, supporting problem solving, and identifying emerging needs, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist will help strengthen program consistency and responsiveness. Lessons learned through these interactions will inform improved practices and contribute to OCAP’s continued evolution.

The role also supports the advancement of modern digital communication tools that enhance accessibility of program information. The incumbent will utilize analytical and visualization platforms, such as ArcGIS and Microsoft Power BI, contributing to clearer communication of complex concepts and improved transparency across OCAP’s work.

This position offers an opportunity to apply strong leadership, advanced technical expertise, and collaborative skills to one of CARB’s most community driven programs, helping shape approaches that support cleaner air and healthier communities across California.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full\-time opportunity available for a **Water Quality Regional Manager (Natural Resource Protection and Sustainability Manager 2\)**. Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

**The Agency:**


The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources. At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission\-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.


The Water Quality Division has a critical role in achieving the Department’s mission by developing policy, implementation tools, and implementation priorities for improving and protecting the quality of water in Oregon’s waterways. The Water Quality Division works cooperatively with the Department’s three regional offices and the Laboratory to deliver programs and services that protect and enhance the quality of the waters of the state to protect public health and the environment.


The Regional Divisions are responsible for implementation of Water Quality, Air Quality, and Waste Management and Cleanup Programs. The Regions provide the following services: compliance inspection of regulated entities; enforcement of permit requirements and administrative rules; issuance of air, water, and solid waste permits; investigation of complaints; issuance of subsurface permits; response to spills or other incidents with environmental impacts; direct contact and liaison with other governmental entities, industries, and the public; and technical assistance to regulated entities and the public. The Regions consist of Northwest, Eastern, and Western Region. This position is in Eastern Region and focuses on the Water Quality Program.


For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

You will lead and manage the Eastern Region’s environmental programs related primarily to TMDL and nonpoint source water quality activities, 401 Water Quality Certification Dredge and Fill and Hydro programs, the statewide Water Integration Team, and regional stormwater permitting and compliance activities. Your work will include contributing to, and collaborating on, development of statewide program goals and objectives and development of regional and staff\-specific goals. You will identify, prioritize, and schedule work; hire, manage, lead, and coach technical and professional staff; resolve difficult technical and/or administrative problems; monitor goal progress; and track and ensure timeliness and responsiveness to the public and regulated community.

These competencies show up in your day\-to\-day work through:

* Supporting staff with the tools, resources, and information they need to succeed.

* Setting clear work objectives, goals, and expectations, and addressing performance with timeliness, care, and accountability.
* Creating belonging by fostering team cohesion, encouraging collaboration, and helping ensure staff understand each other’s roles and can step in to support one another when needed.

At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Water Quality Division has a critical role in achieving the Department’s mission by developing policy, implementation tools, and implementation priorities for improving and protecting the quality of water in Oregon’s waterways. The Water Quality Division works cooperatively with the Department’s three regional offices and the Laboratory to deliver programs and services that protect and enhance the quality of the waters of the state to protect public health and the environment.

The Regional Divisions are responsible for implementation of Water Quality, Air Quality, and Waste Management and Cleanup Programs. The Regions provide the following services: compliance inspection of regulated entities; enforcement of permit requirements and administrative rules; issuance of air, water, and solid waste permits; investigation of complaints; issuance of subsurface permits; response to spills or other incidents with environmental impacts; direct contact and liaison with other governmental entities, industries, and the public; and technical assistance to regulated entities and the public. The Regions consist of Northwest, Eastern, and Western Region. This position is in Eastern Region and focuses on the Water Quality Program.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will lead and manage the Eastern Region’s environmental programs related primarily to TMDL and nonpoint source water quality activities, 401 Water Quality Certification Dredge and Fill and Hydro programs, the statewide Water Integration Team, and regional stormwater permitting and compliance activities. Your work will include contributing to, and collaborating on, development of statewide program goals and objectives and development of regional and staff-specific goals. You will identify, prioritize, and schedule work; hire, manage, lead, and coach technical and professional staff; resolve difficult technical and/or administrative problems; monitor goal progress; and track and ensure timeliness and responsiveness to the public and regulated community.

As a manager and people-centered leader, you will be expected to demonstrate, and model for others, the following competencies: proactive communication, innovation, intentional engagement, mentoring and developing others, stewardship of state resources, and business acumen. These competencies show up in your day-to-day work through:

Supporting staff with the tools, resources, and information they need to succeed.
Coaching, mentoring, and motivating staff through regular check-ins, thoughtful guidance, and opportunities for skill development and career growth.
Setting clear work objectives, goals, and expectations, and addressing performance with timeliness, care, and accountability.
Creating belonging by fostering team cohesion, encouraging collaboration, and helping ensure staff understand each other’s roles and can step in to support one another when needed.

Desired Attributes/Skills

If you have these qualities, let us know! Candidates who are most competitive will reflect the following:

Demonstrated commitment to promoting and enhancing diversity; proven experience developing and implementing diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives; commitment to navigating and facilitating a psychologically safe, culturally responsive, and respectful workplace through a trauma-informed approach.
Experience working with diverse groups and communities; skill and experience in communication and outreach to underrepresented communities; ability to build partnerships across diverse community and partner groups and interests.
Experience building and supporting high-performing, collaborative, and inclusive teams that appreciate and encourage diverse thinking and foster an inclusive culture of belonging; proven experience fostering teamwork among direct-report employees; experience coaching, mentoring, and motivating direct-report employees and peers through inclusivity, equity, and kindness.
Skill in cultivating positive relationships across diverse teams while addressing workplace dynamics with professionalism and cultural sensitivity.
Supervisory management experience in a natural resource or environmental program; supervisory management experience in a government agency or government organization; understanding of or experience working with labor unions, particularly in a government setting.
Experience managing a department with water quality responsibilities, including program and strategic planning; knowledge of the federal and state laws governing water quality and natural resources management; familiarity with regulatory programs involving permitting, inspections, and compliance; familiarity with Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs) and nonpoint sources.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate emerging environmental programmatic priorities with both statewide and national implications; public policy and program development experience in leading discussions with external parties and agency responsibilities to protect human health and the environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead both technical and program development teams using data collection, goal setting, measure design, and report development to address statewide environmental challenges and opportunities.
Ability and experience managing human, financial, and informational resources in a manner that instills employee and public trust and accomplishes the organization's mission.
Experience in strategic planning, plan implementation, succession planning, outcome-based management, and change management; champions process improvement.
Demonstrated skill in advising executives and other decision-makers; political awareness; ability to communicate clearly and effectively in stressful situations, such as with permittees and internal and external partners; excellent verbal and written communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications: 6 years of supervision, management, or progressively related experience or 3 years of related experience and a Bachelor’s degree.

What’s in it for you!

Benefits

DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. You will receive a comprehensive, competitive, and affordable benefits, leave, and wellness package, including:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
11 paid holidays
10 hours of vacation per month, eligible to be used as accrued
8 hours of sick leave per month, eligible to be used as accrued
24 hours of personal business leave per fiscal year, eligible to be used after 6 months of service
Optional life insurance packages
Flexible spending accounts
Membership in the Oregon Public Employees Retirement System (PERS)
Optional deferred compensation retirement program
Opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF)
Continuous growth and development opportunities
Opportunities to serve your community and make an impact through meaningful work
A healthy work/life balance, including flexible schedules and hybrid work options for many positions

This is a full-time, management service supervisory position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

Working Conditions

DEQ believes in a diverse and inclusive work environment. All employees are expected to contribute to a work environment that collectively values and benefits from respecting its diversity and promotes a culture of inclusiveness.

This position will be based out of DEQ’s Bend, Klamath Falls, or Pendleton office; however, the successful candidate may be eligible for hybrid work. The logistics of hybrid work will need to be worked out with the Hiring Manager prior to your hire and may be changed at any time given specific job duties and business needs. DEQ will provide necessary hardware (laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cell phone) for an employee to successfully work from home. At DEQ sites, you will have access to a workspace, however, it may be shared with other employees.

Please note: new hires must report in-person a minimum of 2 days per week for at least their first 6 months of employment with DEQ for training purposes and relationship building.

Most work is performed in a professional office setting with multiple demands on time. There is frequent work under tight deadlines. There will be occasional in-state travel between regional offices and to headquarters in Portland for meetings to ensure efficient, effective operation of the Eastern Region Water Quality program and to successfully supervise employees located throughout the region. This position also requires occasional travel on official State business for seminars, workshops, conferences, site visits, trainings, and public hearings, some of which may involve evening work, weekend work, and/or overnight stays. There may be extended working hours during legislative sessions and emergencies. During site visits, there is the potential for exposure to adverse weather conditions, pollutants, chemicals, contaminated soil and water, fumes, airborne contaminants, fall or tripping hazards, stairs, kneeling, crouching, climbing, and substantial walking.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for leading and managing all EHS programs within a lithium-ion battery manufacturing environment. This is a hands-on, standalone role requiring a self-motivated professional who can independently develop, implement, and maintain safety and environmental compliance programs while supporting daily manufacturing operations. The EHS Specialist will ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, and local regulatory requirements, with specific focus on chemical handling, lithium battery safety, hazardous waste management, and industrial risk prevention.

Key responsibilities

Serve as the primary EHS representative for the facility and the on-site safety resource.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve EHS policies, procedures, and training programs.
Promote a proactive safety culture across manufacturing, warehouse, and engineering teams.

Regulatory Compliance

Ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, state/local regulations, and industry best practices.
Maintain required EHS documentation including SDS management, incident logs, inspections, and permits.
Support regulatory audits and serve as the main contact for external agencies.

Manufacturing & Chemical Safety

Oversee safe handling and storage of lithium-ion battery materials, including electrolytes, solvents, and powders.
Implement controls for fire prevention, thermal runaway risks, and emergency response procedures.
Conduct job hazard analyses (JHAs) and risk assessments for production activities.

Compliance & audit readiness

Ensure document control practices support compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100 (if applicable), and internal ALE quality system requirements.
Support EHS-related documentation aligned with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 where applicable.
Maintain controlled records in an audit-ready state with complete approval and traceability history.
Support internal, customer, and external audits by providing controlled documents and records promptly.

Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Manage hazardous waste programs including labeling, storage, accumulation areas, and disposal coordination.
Ensure compliance with DOT requirements for shipping lithium batteries and hazardous materials (UN 3480/3481).
Coordinate environmental reporting and waste reduction initiatives.

Training & Employee Engagement

Conduct EHS onboarding and recurring training (PPE, chemical safety, lockout/tagout, emergency response, etc.).
Lead safety meetings, toolbox talks, and incident prevention initiatives.
Provide hands-on coaching to employees on safe work practices

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Lead investigations for near-misses, injuries, spills, or safety events.
Track corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Monitor site safety performance metrics and recommend improvements.

Emergency Preparedness

Maintain emergency response plans including fire protection, chemical spill response, evacuation procedures, and first aid readiness.
Coordinate drills and ensure emergency equipment is inspected and functional.

Daily On-the-Floor Support

Perform routine safety inspections and audits in production and warehouse areas.
Partner closely with operations leadership to address safety concerns in real time.
Support implementation of 5S and safe manufacturing practices.

Qualification

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and safety management systems.
Ability to work independently in a one-person EHS role and manage multiple priorities.
Experience in lithium-ion battery, chemical, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing.
Knowledge of hazardous material shipping and storage regulations (DOT/IATA).
Familiarity with ISO 14001 or ISO 45001 standards.
HAZWOPER or other relevant certifications (a plus).

Work Environment and Physical requirements

Manufacturing facility with exposure to chemicals, powered industrial equipment, and regulated battery materials.
Requires use of PPE and adherence to strict safety protocols.
May involve occasional lifting, walking production floors, and responding to urgent safety needs.
Frequent bending, squatting, reaching, and climbing.
Ability to lift up to 35 lbs.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to work safely

jobs.description:
**Come Work With Us**  

  

*Be Exceptional. Deliver Excellence. Make A Difference.*

LimnoTech is a leading environmental engineering and science firm with clients who face water\-related problems that are more challenging and costly than ever before. It is our job to help our clients make decisions based on the best available science and real\-world constraints.  

  

At LimnoTech, our values are to: honor the science, lead through innovation, act through partnership, commit to the long\-term, and pursue big, bold actions. Are you ready to join a team of smart, talented people who are motivated every day to deliver excellence and make a difference for our clients, our partners, and the environment?

  

LimnoTech is seeking an experienced sediment remediation specialist to lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. The selected candidate will be based in one of LimnoTech's primary office locations (Ann Arbor, Los Angeles, Oakdale, or DC). Come work with us!  

  

Responsibilities  

  

The Senior Sediment Remediation Specialist will lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. This senior role requires a seasoned professional to provide technical, managerial, regulatory, and business development support to LimnoTech’s existing contaminated sediments practice. Typical job responsibilities include the following, depending on individual ability, skills, and experience:  

* Leading and overseeing technical work for the full lifecycle of sediment projects, which may include developing site characterization, remedial investigation (RI), and feasibility study (FS) plans; overseeing multi\-media sampling programs (sediment, water, biota, etc.); data interpretation (geostatistics, fingerprinting, etc.); numerical modeling (hydrodynamic, contaminant fate and transport, etc.); developing conceptual site models; evaluating and implementing remedial alternatives (dredging, capping, MNR, etc.); remedial cost estimating; and translating complex scientific findings into high quality technical written/verbal deliverables. Litigation support and expert witness experience is desirable.
* Managing projects through the full project management life cycle, including developing scopes of work, managing budgets, leading and mentoring project teams, coordinating with multi\-disciplinary teams of scientist, engineers, regulators, and responsible parties, delivering high quality deliverables on time and on budget, and client management.
* Providing regulatory expertise on contaminated sediment projects (e.g.: CERCLA, RCRA, or local state programs), which may include agency negotiations.
* Leading and participating in marketing and business development activities, which may include tracking and pursuing relevant requests for proposals, developing marketing documents (quals packages, project profiles, web articles, etc.), cultivating and nurturing client and partner relationships, and actively participating at relevant conferences (e.g.: Battelle).

  

Qualifications  

  

The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of a Bachelor of Science degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or a closely related physical science discipline with 10 or more years of experience in the field. A Master’s degree or Ph.D. is strongly preferred, as the role demands a deep understanding of complex contaminant transport, sediment geochronology, and geochemical partitioning.
* For engineering applicants, an active Professional Engineer (PE) license is expected; for scientists, a Professional Geologist (PG) or related credentials would be highly valued, demonstrating a commitment to professional standards and the ability to seal technical documents.
* In addition to formal academic credentials, specialized training in hydrodynamic modeling or statistical data analysis is a significant advantage.
* Candidates must also have completed the 40\-hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification with current annual refreshers, ensuring they are qualified to oversee field activities at hazardous waste sites.
* Continuous education through participation in industry organizations, such as the Battelle Sediment Conference or ITRC technical teams, is encouraged to ensure the firm remains at the forefront of emerging remediation technologies and evolving regulatory frameworks.
* A demonstrated interest or experience in urban waterfront restoration, engineering with nature, or nature\-based solutions is a plus.
* Must be legally able to work in the U.S. for any employer (proper documentation is required).

  

Compensation  

  

LimnoTech rewards high achievement within a supportive working community. Individual achievement is rewarded through a unique merit review process based on recommendations from colleagues at all levels of the company, plus positive feedback from clients. This system drives pay increases and opportunities for increased project and corporate responsibility. We track individual progress annually to ensure competitiveness within our industry and identify opportunities for targeted professional development.
